service_intro_paragraph_1.value: Skin is generally classified into few categories: normal, dry, oily, and combination. There are also special categories like sensitive and pigmentation skins. Your skin type can change as you age, and other factors like genetics and even illness can play a part.

service_intro_paragraph_2.value:
It’s multi-factorial. Most people have normal skin when they are born, but as they grow up, various factors including habit, lifestyle, environmental and even genetic composition will affect the skin and change its characteristics resulting in various categories that we have.

Normal skin, which has a good balance of moisture, small pores and an even tone, is the goal of most skin care regimens. To maintain its good condition, it’s important to minimize its exposure to the sun and other environmental factors. It’s also important to have good habit and lifestyle.

service_sections_0_heading.value: Treatments for Dry, Thin, Matured, Uneven Tone & Dull Skin

service_sections_0_body.value:
Dry skin suffers from a lack of natural moisture — there’s little oil to act as a surface barrier and lock in moisture. People with dry skin feel tightness about their face, and their skin is often irritated. Flaking is another symptom, but it’s not always a sure sign of dry skin.

Sometimes, severely dry skin can become itchy and painful, leading to a condition called eczema. Treatment of certain medical conditions can sometimes lead to dry skin.

For example, breast cancer treatment may stop hormone production which could in turn affect the quality of your skin.

It might throw people into a menopausal situation at an early age as the oil production stops prematurely. Naturally-occurring menopause can have the same effect; most women begin to experience drier skin as they hit their late forties.

service_sections_1_body.value:
Oily skin is identified by an excess of oil (the technical term is sebum) on the face. Some people with oily skin begin to feel greasy only a few hours after washing.

A very oily person would feel the need to wash their face between noon and 5 p.m., because oil has built up during the day. Oily skin can be an inherited trait, but it can also be caused by puberty, which causes oil glands to go into overdrive.

You may also notice more oil on your “T-zone” because of all the oil glands in the forehead, nose, and chin.

service_sections_1_items_5_text.value: For rough, oily & dehydrated skin. 2 in 1 treatment which effectively removed dead skin cells, smoothen large pores, scar and evening skin. Tone plus the special H2O Crystal mask instantly replace high moisture to improve dehydration problem.

service_sections_2_body.value:
From the sun to hormonal changes, many factors can cause skin pigmentation. These include:

  • Genetics. Some people are born with more freckles than others. Similarly, the same goes for larger areas of darker skin from pigmentation. It is also more common among people who have darker skin, such as those with an Asian, Indian, Latin, Middle Eastern, or Mediterranean background. Their skin often has more melanocytes, the skin cells that produce pigment.
  • Sun damage. Ultraviolet rays from the sun will cause the skin to produce more melanocytes, which leads to the dark spots commonly called age spots or liver spots. Prescription drugs may also make the skin more sensitive to the sun causing skin pigmentation.
  • Hormonal changes in women. This can also stimulate more skin pigment to be produced. Birth control pills and hormone replacement therapy may also cause these skin changes.
  • Skin irritation. People with darker skin may get some pigmentation after acne or psoriasis. And for some people, using skin care products that irritate the skin will cause the skin to produce more pigment and cause dark patches. Even rubbing and itching an area of the skin can make it darker.

If the pigmentation is a result of hormonal changes, your skin may go back to normal at the end of your pregnancy or when you stop taking birth control pills or hormone replacement therapy. In other cases, there are treatments that our consultant can help recommend for your skin condition.

service_intro_heading.value: Remove your unwanted hair in safe, fast & effective way!

service_intro_paragraph_1.value: Hair is composed of protein. The appearance can be a sign of age and health. It also protects the skin and head against trauma and UV light. Hair insulates the skin against temperature changes and is a barrier to foreign objects. All hair is dead protein. Depending on the locations, hair may grow on certain parts of the face and body that are not desirable.

service_sections_0_body.value:
It involves removing hair at all areas like underarm, upper lip, arm, leg, bikini etc. This method works by applying wax to the skin, which sticks to hairs. The wax is then quickly ripped off (some wax need to go with cloth strip, some without), pulling the hairs out with it.

The procedure is relatively quick, so even larger areas like the legs can be waxed in a trivial amount of time. However, because the wax needs to be able to stick to the hair, hair needs to be at least a quarter of an inch long before waxing.

This means that hair needs to be given some time to grow out between waxes. It usually takes about two to four weeks for hair to grow back. Waxing is a more economical way for hair removal.

service_sections_1_body.value:
It is to use the Photopneumatic therapy. During the treatment, a hand piece is gently placed on the skin. In a fraction of a second, a vacuum gently draws the skin into the treatment tip bringing the targets such as hair follicles closer to the skin’s surface.

A painless light is applied that sends highly efficient photons to the target at 4-5 times the standard rate. Because the hair follicles are closer to the light, a lower energy can be used, providing an overall safer, painless procedure that’s extremely fast and effective.

We recommend typically 6-12 treatments to achieve most effective result to achieve average hair reduction of up to 88%. Our clients are extremely satisfied with the treatment. Overall, this therapy offers a safe, rapid and effective method for long-term hair reduction.

But early removal may prevent them from developing into cancer at some future date. Most of the moles make their appearance at sensitive parts of the body and requires special medical attention if they become painful, if they itch, or if they suddenly change in size, shape or color.

service_sections_0_items_1_text.value: A viral infection caused by the Papilloma virus. These growths are caused by a virus infection of the epidermis. In this location, they are known as plantar warts. Warts are often transmitted from one member of the family to another. Warts can spread by scratching, or by shaving, and by brushing the hair. Because warts can spread rapidly on face or around the neck, to painful areas, such as the area around the fingernails, and because they may become disfiguring, it is best to remove them at early stage whenever they appear.

service_sections_0_items_2_text.value: These are brown to black growths on the face and body. They are usually present on the skin of people over 40 years old. privacy-policy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy-policy.content:
Last updated: [27 Oct 2026]

Impression Beauty ("we", "us") respects your privacy. This policy explains what personal data we collect, why we collect it, how we look after it, and what choices you have. It applies when you visit our website, book an appointment, visit our salon at Clarke Quay Central, or buy from our online shop. [CONFIRM registered company name and UEN]

1. What personal data we collect

Depending on how you deal with us, we may collect:

  • Contact details: your name, mobile number, email address and, for shop orders, your delivery address.
  • Appointment details: the services you book, dates and times, and your preferences.
  • Health and skin information: details you share with us so we can advise you and carry out treatments safely, such as allergies, skin conditions, pregnancy, medication, and relevant medical history.
  • Treatment records: notes on your consultations, treatments and aftercare advice.
  • Payment details: for online orders, payments are processed by our payment provider. We do not store your full card number. [CONFIRM payment provider]
  • Website data: technical information such as your IP address, browser type, pages visited and cookie data.
  • Messages: what you send us by phone, email, WhatsApp, social media or our website forms. [CONFIRM channels used]

We do not ask for your NRIC number unless the law requires it. [CONFIRM]

2. Why we collect and use your data

We use your personal data to:

  • book, confirm, change and remind you of appointments
  • assess your skin and recommend suitable treatments
  • carry out treatments safely, and keep a record of them
  • process payments and online shop orders, including delivery and returns
  • respond to your questions and feedback
  • send you information about promotions, new services and products, where you have agreed to receive it
  • improve our website and services
  • meet legal and regulatory requirements, and protect our legal rights

3. Consent

We collect, use and disclose your personal data with your consent, or where the PDPA allows us to do so without it. By giving us your details, making a booking or using our services, you agree to the uses described in this policy. You can withdraw your consent at any time (see Section 9).

4. Marketing messages

You may contact us at any time to:
